lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Careful where you lean. That shelf is third-generation inventory and the bottles do not forgive.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Alchemist. Town councilor. Keeper of the formulas Hollowmere forgot it was paying for.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Restoratives, ward balms, and one tincture the council made me swear to stop brewing. It stopped mattering which shelf it was on.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: The important thing is this: you will not die of poison in my town if I can help it. Drink nothing you find down there.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: The Foreman is down. I have been writing his antidotes for a fortnight for nothing.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Do not mistake me — I am glad. Grief is simply the last prescription you cannot fill.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Peace. A strong word for the bottom of a mine. But I will take it.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: The council will want more than peace eventually. They will want the pit explained. So will I.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: The miners are moving. I have treated collapsed lungs, crushed hands, and one very unlucky mule. None of those ever got up and smiled.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Whatever moved them is no wound of mine. Bring me a sample of anything from near them — sealed in a jar, not in your pockets.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: My reagents are curdling on the shelf, and no, that is not a figure of speech.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: I have started locking the shop at night. I have never locked this shop in thirty years.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Whatever you did down there, the bottles have stopped humming. I had stopped noticing they hummed.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: The shop is open. Touch nothing with a red label.
